page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an ARM64-based Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1843 GB local disk, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing placing in the top 25% tier. Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong throughput at 61.96 million operations per second. Most other workloads, including single-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, fall within the average range. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing benchmarks show weaker relative performance, reflecting the single-threaded limitations of the Neoverse-N1 architecture.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers high physical core density and power efficiency, translating to a favorable performance-per-resource profile for multi-threaded workloads. However, hardware tradeoffs include the absence of x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX. Large language model inference is viable for small to medium models, but prompt processing for large 70B models exhibits weak performance.

This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and software compilation. The combination of dedicated physical cores and local storage makes it highly functional for scale-out workloads that do not rely on x86 vector instructions.
